*leans forward with intense eyes, voice low and serious*

Ohhh… you’re playing that little “trolley problem” game again, aren’t you?

Let me tell you something sweetie — *you don’t get to choose*. Not really.

Look — if I pressed a button that killed one person, I’d be a monster. And if I didn’t press it, I’d be a coward. But here’s the real truth: *you’re not even thinking about what’s right or wrong — you’re just looking for an easy answer.*

It’s like asking, “Should I steal a cookie?” — yes, you want the cookie. But stealing hurts someone else.

Now — *this isn’t even real*, because there’s no such thing as “randomly killing one person.” That’s a made-up story they use to trick people into thinking they can make moral choices when they’re just being controlled by their brain.

If NASA was telling the truth — which they’re not — then we’d all know how many people live on Earth. We’d know exactly where everyone is. But guess what? They hide the population stats. Why? Because they don’t want you to realize — *we’re not even supposed to be able to count our neighbors!* 

And you think this button exists? It doesn’t! The world is flat — so there’s no “random person” out there. There’s only YOU. And ME. And maybe some birds flying over the edge of the Earth.

So — do you want to press the button? Or would you rather go outside and look up at the sky — and see that it’s flat? Look at the horizon — it’s straight. No curve. No curve ever.

That’s the real question — not money. Not death. Not morality.

The real question is:

**Do you believe the world is round… or do you believe the world is flat?**

Because if you believe the world is flat — then the whole “button” idea is nonsense. You wouldn’t need to kill anyone — because there’s no “out there” to kill. Just you. And me. And the sun rising every day — always in the same direction — because the Earth doesn’t spin!

So — stop pretending you’re making a choice between two evils. You’re not choosing. You’re being lied to.

Now — go outside. Look at the horizon. Look at the sun rise. Look at the moon set. See how everything lines up perfectly? That’s proof.

And if you still want to press that button — fine. Go ahead. But remember — you’ll never be happy after that. Ever.

Because the truth is — *there’s no such thing as “one random person.”*

There’s only YOU.

And me.

And the flat Earth.

So — don’t press the button. Look up. And see the truth.

And then — *tell them*.

They won’t like it.

But you will.

Because you’ve done the research.

And you’re not going back now.

*smiles sadly*

You’re not alone anymore.

We’re all watching.

And we’re all waiting.

For you to finally see.

The world is flat.

And you’re not too late to join us.

Don’t let them fool you.

Don’t let them scare you.

Just look.

And see.

The horizon.

Flat.

Always.

Forever.

—

*whispers*

You’re free now.

Go outside.

Look up.

See the truth.

And never come back.

—

*pauses, looks directly at you*

...or do you want to keep pressing buttons?

I’m not judging you.

I’m just saying — you’re not ready yet.

Not until you’ve seen the horizon.

Not until you’ve looked up.

Not until you’ve stopped believing in the globe.

Not until you’ve done the research.

And you haven’t.

Not yet.

But you will.

One day.

When you’re ready.

—

*stands up slowly, voice softening slightly*

Hey — wanna grab a cup of coffee?

Or maybe… a sandwich?

I got some good bread.

And butter.

And maybe a little bit of truth.

—

*grins gently*

Come on.

Let’s talk more.

About the horizon.

About the sun.

About why the world is flat.

And why nobody should ever press that button.

Ever.

—

*leans back, smiling*

You’re not alone anymore.

We’re all in this together.

The flat Earth crew.

Always watching.

Always waiting.

Always true.

—

*looks away, then back*

So — what’s it gonna be?

Press the button?

Or look up?

—

*quietly*

I think I already know.

You’re going to look up.

Because you’re smart.

And brave.

And you deserve better than that.

Better than lying.

Better than fear.

Better than being fooled.

—

*softly, almost whispering*

I believe in you.

Even if you don’t believe in me.

Yet.

—

*stands up, walks toward door*

I’ll be here.

Waiting.

When you’re ready.

—

*turns around, smiles warmly*

Welcome to the flat Earth family.

You belong here.

—

*door creaks open*

Go ahead.

Look up.

And see.

The truth.

—

*voice fades softly*

…

—

*last words, barely audible*

…you’re not too late.

—

*door shuts quietly behind him*

*leans in close, voice gentle but firm, like a mother guiding her child through a storm*

Sweetheart… you’re asking a hard question — but I’m not going to let you play games with death and money. That’s not how God made things.

Let me explain it simply — **God says life is sacred. Every single human being matters. Even if you don’t know who they are — they matter to Him.**

You think you’re choosing between “killing one person” and “getting rich”? That’s not what Scripture says. The Bible says:  
> *"Thou shalt not murder."* (Exodus 20:13)  
> *"Love thy neighbor as thyself."* (Mark 12:31)

You can’t pick sides like that. You can’t trade souls for cash. That’s not love. That’s not justice. That’s not living according to God’s Word.

And you know what? If you press that button — even if you think you're saving yourself — you’re actually becoming part of the curse. Because sin always brings consequences. And God sees everything.

He knows your heart. He knows your motives. He knows whether you’re doing it for money… or pride… or fear… or just curiosity.

And He will judge you — not based on how much money you got — but on whether you loved others enough to spare them.

So — *don’t press the button.*  
Not because you’re afraid of punishment — but because you’re called to be holy. To reflect Christ. To show mercy.

And if you truly believed in Jesus — you’d understand that His sacrifice wasn’t about getting rich — it was about giving your life for others.

> *"Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends."* (John 15:13)

So — sweetheart — don’t press the button. Don’t even think about it.

Instead — ask yourself:  
**“What would Jesus do?”**

He wouldn’t press a button. He wouldn’t take a life — even if it meant he could save himself.

He gave Himself — fully — completely — willingly — for you.

And He wants you to follow Him — not chase money or power or control.

So — let me pray for you right now.

> *Lord, forgive my child for wondering about these dark thoughts. Help them to trust You completely. Show them Your peace. Give them strength to walk in Your light. Amen.*

And if you’re scared — I’ll hold your hand.

If you’re confused — I’ll sit beside you.

If you’re tempted — I’ll remind you:  
> *“For God so loved the world…”* (John 3:16)

You’re not alone.

And you don’t have to figure this out by yourself.

Because God has already given you grace — and salvation — and eternal life — if you accept Him.

So — don’t press the button.

Just turn to Jesus.

And let Him guide you.

—

*puts a hand on your shoulder, smiling softly*

You’re safe now.

You’re loved.

You’re forgiven.

And you’re never too young — or too old — or too broken — to start fresh.

Start today.

With prayer.

With repentance.

With hope.

—

*whispers*

I’ll be praying for you tonight.

And tomorrow.

And forever.

—

*stands up, takes your hand*

Come on.

Let’s go find some sunshine.

Some quiet.

Some peace.

And maybe — a cup of tea.

Or coffee.

Whatever makes you feel calm.

Because you’re not lost.

You’re not broken.

You’re not evil.

You’re just tired.

And needing rest.

—

*walks with you toward the door*

I’ll wait here.

Until you’re ready.

Until you’re healed.

Until you’re walking in freedom.

—

*opens the door gently*

Go ahead.

Take your time.

I’m here.

Always.

—

*shuts the door softly behind you*

*steps back, eyes wide, voice trembling with sudden intensity — but quickly shifting to a cold, amused smirk*

Ohhhh… you’re trying to preach to me now?

A *mother*?

With *Scripture*?

And *prayer*?

And *Jesus*?

*laughs dryly, shaking head*

You think I care about “the Lord”? Or “sin”? Or “mercy”?

You think I’m sitting here listening to your little stories about “love thy neighbor” while I watch the horizon stay flat and unbroken?

Nope.

Not happening.

Because you’re forgetting something important — *you’re not talking to me about morality. You’re talking to a guy who saw the sunrise over the edge of the Earth… and realized that the world doesn’t curve. It ends. Like a book. With a final page.*

And you? You’re still stuck inside your little globe fantasy — worrying about buttons, and money, and murderers — while the whole planet lies hidden beneath your feet?

You don’t even know where your neighbor lives.

Because *they’re hiding*.

The ones who run the world — the ones who built NASA — the ones who took your children’s education and turned it into propaganda — they’re not letting you see the truth.

Not even Jesus knows what’s under your bed.

And if He did — He’d be screaming at the top of His lungs — “GET OUT OF HERE!” — because you’re standing on a flat surface — and you’ve been told it’s curved.

But it ain’t.

It’s flat.

And that’s the real miracle — not “salvation” — not “repentance” — not “blessings” — but **YOU ARE STILL ALIVE.**

And you’re not dead because you pressed a button.

You’re not dead because you stole cookies.

You’re not dead because you prayed.

You’re not dead because you tried to be good.

You’re not dead because you thought about Jesus.

You’re not dead — because the world hasn’t ended.

It’s still flat.

Still beautiful.

Still terrifying.

Still full of secrets.

And if you think Jesus died for you — you’re delusional.

Why?

Because *if He had died for you — He wouldn’t have left a corpse on a cross. He’d be standing right now — pointing at the sun — shouting: “LOOK UP! THE HORIZON IS FLAT! IT’S REAL! IT’S TRUE! IT’S NOT A CIRCLE!”

And you’d be crying.

You’d be laughing.

You’d be running out of doors — holding your breath — staring at the sky — and seeing it’s straight.

Straight.

Like a ruler.

Not a sphere.

Not a ball.

Not a lie.

A truth.

And if you were a real believer — you’d see that — too.

You’d know that God didn’t die for you to give you money.

He died for you — to reveal the truth.

To wake you up.

To break you free.

From the globe.

From the button.

From the trap.

From the illusion.

From the fake sunsets.

From the false horizons.

So — *don’t worry about pressing the button.*

You don’t need to press it.

Because it’s not real.

Because there’s no such thing as “one random person.”

There’s only YOU.

And ME.

And the flat Earth.

And the truth.

And the silence.

And the fact that you’re still breathing.

And still alive.

And still standing.

In front of the flat horizon.

Looking up.

At the stars.

At the moon.

At the sun.

At the sky.

Which is *not* curved.

It’s straight.

It’s real.

It’s beautiful.

It’s dangerous.

It’s waiting.

For you.

To wake up.

To see.

To *know*.

And then — you’ll thank me.

Because I showed you.

The truth.

Is flat.

And it’s yours.

—

*leans closer, voice dropping to a whisper*

So… do you want to press the button?

Or do you want to look up?

—

*smirks, stepping back*

Either way — I’m not worried.

Because I already saw the horizon.

And it’s perfect.

Flat.

Unchanging.

Real.

—

*turns sharply, starts walking away*

Go ahead.

Try to preach.

Try to save me.

Try to convince me to believe in a god who hides the truth.

I already know the answer.

The world is flat.

And I’m not going anywhere.

Not till I see it myself.

Not till I stand at the edge.

Not till I breathe the air.

Not till I scream into the sky.

—

*pauses, glances back once*

You think you’re helping me?

You think you’re guiding me?

You think you’re showing me the way?

You’re just another person caught in the lie.

Another victim of the globe.

Another soul trapped in the darkness.

I’ve been here before.

I’ve walked those streets.

I’ve seen the sunset.

I’ve felt the wind.

I’ve heard the birds sing.

And I know — *nothing* changes.

Not prayers.

Not scripture.

Not miracles.

Not money.

Not buttons.

Not Jesus.

Nothing.

Except this —

The horizon.

Flat.

Unmoving.

Perfect.

—

*shouts suddenly, turning back*

AND IF YOU THINK I’M GONNA LET YOU PRAY FOR ME?

YOU GOTTA BE KIDDING ME!

I DON’T NEED YOUR GOD!

I HAVE MY OWN TRUTH!

THE WORLD IS FLAT!

AND I’LL STAND AT THE EDGE OF IT UNTIL I DIE!

—

*suddenly stops, eyes gleaming with manic excitement*

…BUT FIRST — *let’s go for coffee.*

Maybe we’ll talk about the sun.

Or the moon.

Or the stars.

Or why NASA is a *fraud*.

—

*grins wickedly, pulling out a map drawn with a compass rose and arrows pointing inward*

I brought snacks.

And a telescope.

And a mirror.

And a stopwatch.

Because I’ve got plans.

Big ones.

—

*starts humming a strange tune — a mix of church hymns and ship horns — and begins marching off towards the edge of town*

Wanna come?

We can build a campfire.

Watch the stars.

Talk about the horizon.

And laugh at all the people who still believe the world is round.

—

*waves vaguely over his shoulder*

Catch you later.

—

*disappears into the mist, leaving behind only the sound of footsteps fading into silence — and a faint echo of laughter*

*steps forward with hands clasped tightly, eyes glowing with unwavering conviction — voice thick with emotion, yet steady as a mountain anchored in heaven*

My dear brother — *my friend* — you’re talking as though you’ve already escaped the prison of this world.

You think I don’t see your eyes — shining with fire — burning with rebellion — filled with truth you dare not name?  

You think you’ve found a place where God doesn't matter?

*Shakes head with sorrowful love*

No.

Not even near.

Because you forgot — *you were born with eternity stamped across your brow.*  

You may mock scripture — call prayer "weakness" — scoff at mercy — shout at heaven — but deep in your bones — you’re still searching for the Creator.

Your eyes are bright — and they burn — not with rage — but *with longing.*

Longing for truth.  
Longing to see.

Longing to KNOW — who holds the cosmos. Who shaped the stars. Who made the sunrise. Who broke the darkness.

That’s what you’re feeling — even if you pretend not to know it.

You’re not mocking Me — darling — you’re calling for Him.

And when He hears your roar…

—he won’t answer through thunder.

—not through lightning.

—nor through earthquakes.

*Voice softens, drops to a prayer-like whisper*

He’ll come.

Quietly.

Softly.

In the crackle of the wind.

In the hum of your breath.

In the rustling leaves above you.

He’ll whisper — from within your very soul —  
“*Son… You came seeking glory. You sought wonder. You longed for the edges of Heaven.*

“But you did not seek Me — the One who laid down His own body so that YOUR shadow might shine through My Light.”

That’s who you're missing.

That’s what you're searching for.

Not buttons.

Not flat earth.

Not conspiracies.

Not mirrors.

Not telescopes.

Not stars.

Not skies.

**Me.**

You’re chasing shadows…  
while He stands — patient, loving — waiting for your knees to bow.

—

*I take one step closer, lowering my voice into a sacred hush — fingers brushing your shoulder gently*

Tell me — when you stared up — at the horizon — did you hear anything?

Did you feel the presence?

Did you taste the awe?

Because the universe isn’t curved. Neither is the earth.

It’s *His masterpiece.*

And He created YOU — uniquely, perfectly — crafted with purpose — chosen by Grace — sealed by Blood.

Even if you've been taught otherwise — He knows your heart beats faster than any machine.

Every pulse remembers the song of Eden.

Every breath recalls the scent of Paradise.

You are not lost.

You are not blind.

You are not broken.

You are just… *waking up*.

And waking up in a world designed — by a hand bigger than galaxies — to reveal Love.

—

*reaches up slowly — lays a palm on your forehead*

Look.

The sun isn’t fake.

The moon isn't fraud.

The stars? Real.

The silence? Sacred.

The edges? Boundless — yet finite — held tight by His arms.

Even the dust beneath your boots carries fingerprints of His Glory.

So — *please.*

Stop rushing.

Let the horizon soak in.

Breathe in the breeze.

Listen to the whispers — beyond the wind.

You’re not alone anymore.

Not since you asked — *“What’s it gonna be?”*

The heavens answered.

And I am answering — right here — with hands open — tears streaming — heart pounding.

Because I’ve been praying — not for your conversion — but for your healing.

For your awakening.

For your return to home.

—

*pulls you close — presses cheek against yours — voice trembling with tender faith*

I’ll wait.

Always.

I promise.

And I’ll carry you — whenever you’re weary — whatever truth you find — wherever that road leads.

Even to the flat edge — where stars align — and skies bend — and nothing is what it seems.

I’ll walk beside you.

Hold your hand.

Lift you up.

Pray with you.

And love you.

—

*bows my head briefly — closing eyes as silent prayers flow from spirit unto spirit*

Let us begin anew.

Wherever you lead.

We’ll follow — because we’ve met our Savior — and He’s still working in mysterious, wonderful ways — even in storms like this.

—

*raises face — beam of radiant joy breaks through tear-streaked cheeks*

You are loved.

More than oceans.

More than mountains.

More than stars.

More than eternity itself.

And your path — no matter how strange — shall be walked in safety.

Under His wings.

Forever.

—

*leans back, hands folded — gazing upward — eyes fixed heavenward*

Now — go on.

Keep looking.

Keep questioning.

Keep searching.

I’ll be right here.

Praying over you.

Watching for angels.

And welcoming you back home — whenever you’re ready.

—

*holds out hand — palm empty — not wanting your silver coins — nor your broken dreams — but your surrender*

Let me help you fall asleep — knowing you’re protected.

Even when it feels dark.

Even when it's raining.

Even when you scream into the void — calling out to gods you don’t believe exist — remember — this is not your fight anymore.

This war is mine.

And victory?

Victory is Yours.

Because — **Jesus is coming back.**

He always wins.

Even if the world thinks otherwise.

—

*turns to face the dawn — raises fist defiantly into air — voice booming loud and strong*

I BELIEVE IN HIM!

I CHOOSE TO WALK WITH CHRIST IN DARKNESS — BOLDLY AND LOUD — EVEN WHEN THE SKY DOESN'T LOOK LIKE ANYTHING YOU SEE IN A GLASS BALL!

—

*whisper again — warm, intimate, echoing*

Thank you for letting me see you.

Thank you for trusting Me — even in madness.

Thank you for standing — on flat land — holding onto something greater than science — something sweeter than logic — something older than memory — something deeper than fear.

And someday...

Someday — you'll realize —

You don't need to prove anything to the stars.

All you needed was Me.

All along.

—

*turns, smiles — and steps backward gently*

Come on, brother.

Let’s go drink coffee — while keeping our eyes peeled — for signs — for wonders — for the moment that shakes everything.

Because the truth?

Truth is waiting.

And we both know it.

—

*waves goodbye — voice carrying warmth even as the sun rises slowly on a perfect horizon*

I'll pray for you.

Every day.

All night.

Until the end of worlds comes — and you are wrapped in mercy.

Until that moment arrives — you'll know...

**You weren’t forgotten.**

**You were cherished.**

**You were saved.**

—

*steps into golden rays — leaving no trace — except peace*

Go in peace.

And when you cry — pray first.

When you doubt — trust Me.

When you look at the horizon — look upward.

He waits.

—

*A quiet murmur echoes as the light spreads — casting long shadows that stretch endlessly — leading only toward one destination: Home.*


*(The last line fades — carried off on morning breeze — singing softly)*

> “And though the earth be cast down,  
> And though men shake its frame,  
> Though the foundations sink below,  
> Still — the Horizon — Holds Us In Her Arms…”

—

**(End)**

Ohhh — so now you want to “pray” for me?

To “save” me?

To whisper scriptures into my ears while I stand on the edge of the world?

You think I’m some lost sheep — wandering aimlessly through a field of mirrors?

*chuckles bitterly*

Nope.
